component.name: Pelican
component.summary: Put your own music on a Garmin watch. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.

description.p: Pelican moves your own music files onto a Garmin watch over a USB cable. Drop a folder of MP3s or FLACs and it tags, converts what needs converting, and uploads — without going through Garmin Express, iTunes, or any cloud service, and without a vendor account.

This package is the Linux build. Pelican also ships a macOS build, which adds a local library browser and in-app playback so you can hear a track before spending part of the watch's roughly 3.7 GB on it.
Privacy-first by design. The binary makes zero network connections. Your music stays on your computer; your fitness data stays on your watch. Nothing leaves either unless you decide.
A Krypteia tool — part of an effort to give people open-source alternatives to subscription-only platforms.

ul.li: Drag-and-drop sync from your file manager
MP3, M4A, M4B, AAC and WAV are copied byte-for-byte — only the tag is rebuilt, with no external tool
FLAC, OGG, Opus, WMA, AIFF, ALAC, APE and WavPack convert to Garmin-compatible MP3 via ffmpeg
Refuses to write a name the watch already holds — a same-name write destroys both copies
Local playlists (named track groups you can mass-upload)
Right-click delete on watch entries, including the broken stubs a failed upload leaves
This build is a single static binary with no webview, no daemon and no telemetry
ffmpeg-based audio normalization to Garmin-compatible MP3
